title: Rosalind and the Postcard
premise: Seven years ago, Freya Ishikawa fled a scandal that ended her engagement and her career in one night, rebuilding herself as a wedding planner who plans other people's happily-ever-afters while trusting none of them. When a snowstorm traps her at a remote island inn with Callum Reeve — the man she loved and betrayed in their twenties, now the brother of her biggest client — old wounds and older sparks reignite over a single undelivered postcard she never stopped carrying. As the last ferry of the season approaches, Freya must choose between the safe, fragmentary life she's built and risking her whole heart on the one person who knows exactly what it cost her to survive. She boards the ferry alone — then jumps off at the dock and walks back through the snow to him.
about_author: T. M. Halloran is the pen name of a former event coordinator who spent a decade watching love from behind the catering table before turning to write about it. They live on a windswept coast where ferries genuinely do stop running in winter.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya arrives on Greywick Island to plan the wedding of socialite Margot Reeve, armed with checklists and emotional armor. A chance glimpse of the guest list reveals Callum Reeve's name — Margot's brother, the man from her past. The chapter ends with the ferry horn sounding its final departure before the storm closes in. Beat: dread disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Snowed In With Ghosts
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. The storm strands guests at the inn, and Callum recognizes Freya before she can slip away. Their first conversation is all polished small talk over cracked porcelain cups, but every line carries seven years of unfinished business. He notices she still wears the same worn coat. Beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: What the Postcard Said
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Unpacking, Freya's keepsake tin spills, and Callum sees the postcard he sent her the week everything fell apart — never mailed back, edges soft from handling. She deflects with wedding logistics, but the confrontation cracks her composure for the first time. Beat: exposure; the artifact of memory made undeniable.

chapters.title: Rivals at the Dessert Table
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wedding planning forces them into collaboration when the island caterer cancels. Old competitive habits resurface — they were rivals long before they were lovers — and bickering curdles into laughter neither expected. Margot watches them with sharp, suspicious eyes. Beat: warmth sneaking past defenses.

chapters.title: The Version of You I Knew
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. By firelight, Callum tells Freya what the scandal did to him — how he waited for an explanation that never came, and rebuilt himself around the absence. Freya almost tells him why she ran, then retreats. He realizes she's still protecting someone. Beat: intimacy deepening as truth stays withheld.

chapters.title: Margot's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Margot confronts Freya: she knows who Freya is, and if her brother gets hurt again, the wedding — and Freya's career — are finished. Freya agrees to keep distance, then breaks it that same night, finding Callum on the frozen jetty. One kiss, immediately regretted and instantly wanted again. Beat: desire overriding survival instinct.

chapters.title: Why I Ran
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Cornered by Callum's quiet fury after the kiss, Freya finally confesses: she took the fall for her fiancé's fraud to protect her younger sister, trading her name, career, and Callum for a sibling's safety. The postcard was the only piece of her old life she kept. Beat: catharsis; the price of survival named aloud.

chapters.title: Pieces, Not the Whole
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Stunned but not absolved, Callum accuses Freya of doing it again — offering explanations instead of trust, lending pieces of herself while keeping the whole heart locked away. Margot overhears and, unexpectedly, defends Freya, revealing she once made a similar trade. Beat: climax of conflict; love demanding more than history.

chapters.title: The Ice Breaks
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. On the morning the ice thaws enough for the ferry, Freya stands at the gangway with her contract signed and her heart still rationed. Margot hands her the postcard — 'deliver it yourself this time.' Freya hesitates as the horn sounds, sees Callum walking away down the pier, and makes her choice. Beat: the decision point.

chapters.title: Back Through the Snow
chapters.summary: Dual POV converging. Freya jumps ship, crosses the icy dock, and gives Callum not the postcard but the truth she owes: her whole self, unguarded, staying even after the storm lifts. They plan nothing — no wedding, no checklist — just a beginning. Epilogue beat: spring ferry schedule pinned to the inn's wall, two names circled. Beat: belonging earned, not arranged.
